title: Hypercerts
subtitle: Fund the work on a record anyone can check
label: Hypercerts
summary: What a hypercert records, how funders use it, where it runs today, and where a government can use it.
standfirst: Every funder asks projects the same questions and checks the answers from scratch. With AI, a polished application now takes minutes to write and proves little. A hypercert gives a piece of work one public record: what was done, where and when, with the evidence, the reviews and the funding attached. The records live on the AT Protocol, in accounts the projects control, so any funder or tool can read them and add to them.

tools.title: Record the work
tools.promise: One record, added to by many hands
tools.text: A project publishes an activity claim from its own account: what it did, where and when. Others add to it over time. The team posts updates and evidence, a monitoring partner adds measurements, and peers, local people and experts add evaluations. Each signal stays with whoever published it, so the record shows who said what.

tools.title: Fund the work
tools.promise: Each funder starts from what others already know
tools.text: A funder reads the record, chooses which signals to trust and how to weigh them, and adds its own support to the same record. The next funder starts from that history instead of a blank form. Today hypercerts back crowdfunding with matching funds. The same records could carry outcome payments, prizes and milestone bounties.

evidence.caption: to 201 community-led regeneration projects in 56 countries in Ma Earth's third round. Gifts from 11,700+ donors decided how a $1M matching pool was shared.
evidence.source: Ma Earth, Round 3, and the Hypercerts Foundation case study

evidence.caption: published works recorded on the hypercert of PL R&D's 2025 Impact Evaluator Research Retreat in Reykjavík, next to the $140k invested in it.

steps.label: How a record builds up
steps.aside: From one claim to the next funding decision

items.title: Claim
items.text: The project publishes what it did, where and when, from its own account.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: It attaches updates, photos, data and measurements as the work goes on.

items.title: Review
items.text: Peers, local people, experts and certifiers add their own evaluations, under their own names.

items.title: Fund
items.text: Funders record their support and, if they choose, why. The next funder starts from this history.

steps.bar: every signal is a separate record, published by whoever gave it. An evaluator adds an assessment of its own, and only the project can change the project's account.

items.text: Funding rounds for grassroots nature projects, where crowdfunding signals steer the matching pool. Round 4 opens on Earth Day 2027.
Communities log species, sounds and field work from their phones, and publish it as Certs they can take to other apps and funding rounds.
Each edition is a hypercert with its evidence timeline, outputs and funding.

uses.label: Where a government can use them

items.text: Let applicants bring the record they already have, and add your review to it for the next funder.
Match what citizens give to local projects, and let their gifts steer the match.
Release payments when the agreed measurements and evaluations appear on the record.
Publish what a programme funded and what came of it, in a format any auditor or tool can read.
The [government pilot partnership](/areas/economies-governance/programs/government-pilot-partnership/) sets out how we run one with you.

limit.title: A record is not proof
limit.text: A hypercert records a claim. It does not prove it. Trust comes from the evidence attached and from who vouches for it, and a false claim is as easy to publish as a true one. Hypercerts do not decide which work is valuable or whose judgement counts. Each funder chooses which signals to trust.

wayIn.title: Bring us one funding programme
wayIn.text: Tell us about a grant, prize or matching scheme you run, and we will help you put its applications, reviews and payments on hypercerts.
